items.title: MetaboLLM: a metabolomics-specialized large language model for biochemical knowledge integration and predictive metabolite graph construction
items.abstract: MetaboLLM is a specialized large language model for metabolomics that integrates distributed biochemical knowledge. It achieves this through continual pretraining, fine-tuning, and structured retrieval, enabling it to generate accurate biochemical descriptions. These descriptions are then used by MetaboLLM-GIN to construct predictive metabolite graphs, which significantly improve patient-level predictions for various clinical outcomes.

items.title: TRAJDEBUG: Tracing Error Lifecycle to Identify Critical Failures in Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories
items.abstract: TrajDebug is a framework designed to pinpoint the root cause of failures in long, complex trajectories generated by LLM-based agents. It tackles the challenges of scattered evidence and multiple local errors by compressing historical context and tracing the resolution status and impact of each identified error. This allows for the critical attribution of failures to their earliest originating steps.
items.figure_caption: Critical error detection requires grounding errors in long-range context and distinguishing the failure-responsible error from multiple coexisting errors.

items.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Evaluating Benchmarks for Conversational Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel, reference-free framework that leverages LLM judges to assess the quality of conversational agent benchmarks. Its core method involves evaluating benchmark consistency, complexity, and policy coverage, providing actionable diagnostics. The key contribution is a practical approach to reliably identify and improve flawed benchmarks, ensuring more accurate evaluations of conversational agents.

items.title: From Passive Mirrors to Active Agents: Holonic Digital Twins for Physical AI over Networks
items.abstract: This paper proposes Holonic Digital Twins (HDT-Nets) to enable real-time physical AI over networks. Unlike passive digital twins, HDTs are active agents that reason about their environment, allowing for reliable world modeling and long-horizon planning under uncertainty. This framework addresses limitations of current AI in physical systems by leveraging wireless networks for coordinated, context-aware physical intelligence.

items.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
items.abstract: This paper introduces HarnessOpt-Bench, a novel benchmark for evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) in the task of harness optimization. The core method involves an LLM-based optimizer iteratively improving a given LLM agent's surrounding code (harness) based on graded feedback and a limited evaluation budget. The main contribution is providing a standardized protocol to measure LLMs' ability to optimize their own deployment, addressing a gap in current AI system evaluation.
items.figure_caption: Trusted execution for held-out harness optimization. The optimizer can write only the target agent’s harness. It can read the evaluation results and the target task data but not modify them. The optimizer receives per-case development traces and aggregate validation metrics, while test cases and scores remain inaccessible behind the trusted evaluation server. Each candidate is evaluated in isolated, unprivileged sandboxes, and every model call, both the optimizer’s own and the evaluations’, passes through a gateway that enforces model allow-lists and per-scope budgets. The test partition is evaluated only after the optimizer nominates a final candidate. Because held-out data, provider credentials, and budget enforcement are absent from the optimizer’s sandbox, these restrictions are properties of the execution environment rather than instructions the optimizer is expected to follow.

items.title: Improving the Realism of Synthetic Clinical Benchmarks Under Utility Constraints
items.abstract: This paper addresses the issue of synthetic clinical benchmarks being unrealistic despite passing utility checks, particularly in privacy-sensitive healthcare. The core method is to improve benchmark realism while maintaining downstream utility, framing it as a "utility-constrained realism improvement" problem. The contribution lies in proposing and demonstrating a framework to enhance synthetic data realism through metrics like missingness structure and population alignment, ensuring practical usefulness for AI agents.

items.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Nimblemind Multi-Agent System (nMAS), an automated pipeline for engineering heart failure features from electronic health records. nMAS addresses the bottleneck of manual feature engineering by integrating clinical reasoning and evidence traceability. Its core contribution is a rubric-grounded system that generates verified, aggregated features, significantly improving the performance of heart failure prediction models.
items.figure_caption: Overview of the nMAS heart-failure feature-extraction pipeline.

items.title: What Current AI Benchmarks Leave Unmeasured: Modality, Search, Citations, and Implications (for Safety Evaluations)
items.abstract: This paper argues that current AI benchmarks for LLMs are insufficient for safety evaluations because they overlook crucial factors like modality, search capabilities, and citation grounding. By comparing API and chat UI access with and without web search on existing benchmarks, the authors reveal that these unmeasured dimensions significantly impact model behavior and reliability, highlighting a critical gap in current assessment practices.
items.figure_caption: Average per-run accuracy across modalities and search conditions. Error bars represent 95% confidence intervals.

items.title: A Six-Dimensional Taxonomy of Post-Training Adaptation Techniques with Applications in AI Governance
items.abstract: This paper introduces a six-dimensional taxonomy to systematically categorize and understand the diverse landscape of post-training adaptation techniques in machine learning. By organizing methods based on mechanism, goal, data, persistence, scope, and model type, it clarifies distinctions between similar techniques and maps their evolution across different model architectures. This contribution provides a unified framework for analyzing and comparing adaptation strategies, crucial for AI governance and responsible model development.

items.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing LLMs for Rule-Intensive Review of National Standard Documents
items.abstract: This paper introduces GB/T-Bench, the first benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) in reviewing rule-intensive national standard documents. The benchmark utilizes a hierarchical taxonomy to assess LLMs on aspects like document structure, scope, terminology, and normative consistency, identifying 25 specific error types. This work aims to improve LLM performance in professional document review, a task currently reliant on costly human expertise.
items.figure_caption: A GB/T document review case and dataset statistics of GB/T-Bench.

items.title: NeSy-RAG: Neuro-Symbolic RAG for Explainable Question Answering
items.abstract: NeSy-RAG is a neuro-symbolic framework that enhances explainable question answering by augmenting retrieval-based methods. It converts retrieved text into attributable Prolog modules, enabling verifiable reasoning and clear evidence attribution. The system also detects and addresses missing user context by identifying crucial facts needed for accurate query resolution.
items.figure_caption: Overview of the proposed NeSy-RAG framework

items.title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer
items.abstract: This paper introduces RP-OPSD, a novel method for multilingual reasoning transfer in LLMs. It addresses the limitation of existing on-policy self-distillation by focusing distillation efforts on "reasoning pivots" – critical decision points in the reasoning process. RP-OPSD uses the distributional shift between teacher outputs with and without an English reference to identify and guide distillation around these pivots, improving cross-lingual reasoning capabilities.
items.figure_caption: Motivation of reasoning-pivot-guided transfer. Surface variants can preserve the same reasoning state, while pivot drift corrupts downstream reasoning. RP-OPSD uses the distribution gap between the solution-conditioned view q t + q_{t}^{+} and the ablated view q t − q_{t}^{-} to identify reasoning-sensitive tokens. The Frence CoT means ”So we multiply 4 by 3, which makes 12”.

items.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
items.abstract: This paper introduces Programmatic Tool Calling (PTC), a method that allows LLMs to invoke tools as executable Python scripts, enabling more natural chaining and parallelization than traditional JSON calls. Empirically, PTC matches or surpasses JSON tool calling across most tested models on the BFCL v4 benchmark, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for improved agent capabilities.
items.figure_caption: Overview of the two primary paradigms evaluated. In JSON tool calling , the model emits JSON tool-call objects via the API. In programmatic tool calling , it writes a Python script using typed stubs; the agent loop executes it in a subprocess. A filesystem-discovery condition is included as a secondary reference point.
